dg-fmr-hermit-crab-diet.title: FMR Hermit Crab Diet
dg-fmr-hermit-crab-diet.summary: A dry staple food for land hermit crabs, made with food oils to help crabs molt successfully. Feed it alongside a variety of unsalted fresh foods.
rows: Corn meal, soybean meal, alfalfa meal, animal and plant protein products, soybean and coconut oil
Calcium carbonate plus added vitamins and minerals
notes: Give hermit crabs a varied diet: fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, nuts and seeds, all unsalted, along with this food.
warn: Never feed salted foods. The added iodine in table salt is harmful to hermit crabs.

dg-fmr-hermit-crab-treat.title: FMR Hermit Crab Treat (1.5 oz)
dg-fmr-hermit-crab-treat.summary: A fruit-based treat for land hermit crabs that adds variety to their regular diet.
rows: Papaya, coconut, pineapple, sea salt, banana chips, apple, mango, rolled oats and wheat germ
notes: A treat, not a staple. Feed it along with a staple diet and a variety of unsalted fresh foods.

dg-hermit-crab-shell-fancy.title: Hermit Crab Shell (fancy)
dg-hermit-crab-shell-fancy.summary: A spare shell for land hermit crabs. Crabs must move into bigger shells as they grow, so always keep several extras in different sizes and opening shapes.
rows: Measure the width of the shell opening, not the shell length
Keep several spare shells per crab (about 3–6)
Round (turbo), D-shaped and oval openings; crabs have their own preferences
notes: Offer a range of sizes a little larger than each crab's current shell so it can move up when ready.
Natural turbo shells are a favorite of purple pincher crabs.
Never pull a crab out of its shell; let it switch on its own.
warn: Hermit crab welfare groups advise natural, uncoated shells: painted, glazed or varnished shells can harm crabs. If a shell is painted, offer natural shells too.
